extracted.intended_audience: petitioners and stakeholders (environmental groups, industry, state agencies)
extracted.subtask_description: EPA's official response to a TSCA Section 21 petition about chemicals and mixtures used in oil and gas exploration/production (especially hydraulic fracturing), describing legal standards for action, what aspects are granted or denied, and planned procedural steps for rulemaking and stakeholder engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: TSCA section 21(b)(1) 'necessary to issue' standard for section 4 test rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition requesting issuance of a TSCA section 4 test rule must 'set forth sufficient facts to conclude that it is "necessary to issue" the requested TSCA section 4 rule,' as required by TSCA section 21(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA denied the TSCA section 4 request because the petition did not set forth sufficient facts to meet this 'necessary to issue' threshold. This is the legal threshold EPA applies when evaluating a section 4 test-rule petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of TSCA section 8(a) and 8(d) authorities to obtain data
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA decided to partially grant the petition's TSCA section 8(a) and section 8(d) requests and will use TSCA authorities to obtain data on chemical substances and mixtures used in hydraulic fracturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA intends to initiate a proposed rulemaking process under TSCA 8 authorities to obtain data; the resulting proposal will be informed by stakeholder input and existing information, and is intended to gather information to inform EPA's proposal rather than duplicate state programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain records and submit reports (TSCA section 8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition requested that manufacturers and processors be required to develop and maintain records and submit reports to EPA on E&P chemical substances and mixtures and any data on environmental or health effects and exposures pursuant to TSCA section 8(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA has partially granted section 8(a)-type requests for hydraulic fracturing chemicals and will consider design and scope of reporting requirements through stakeholder processes to minimize burdens and avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of health and safety studies (TSCA section 8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition requested that manufacturers, processors and distributors submit health and safety studies related to E&P chemical substances and mixtures pursuant to TSCA section 8(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA indicated it is partially granting 8(d) requests in the context of hydraulic fracturing data collection and will consider implementation details via stakeholder engagement and rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of information on significant adverse reactions (TSCA section 8(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition requested submission of copies of any information related to significant adverse reactions to health or the environment pursuant to TSCA section 8(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition's 8(c) request was noted; EPA's letter describes plans to pursue reporting under certain TSCA authorities but does not state unconditional adoption of the 8(c) requirement outside the stakeholder/rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder process to develop overall approach
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will convene a stakeholder process to develop an overall approach to TSCA reporting requirements for chemicals used in hydraulic fracturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stakeholder process will include states, industry and public interest groups as full partners and will focus on minimizing burdens, leveraging existing information, avoiding duplication, and maximizing transparency and public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize reporting burdens and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Design principle: the approach to reporting requirements should minimize reporting burdens and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA explicitly states the stakeholder dialogue will focus on ways to minimize reporting burdens and costs while obtaining needed data; this is central to the design of any proposed TSCA reporting requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take advantage of existing information and avoid duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Design principle: take advantage of existing information and avoid duplication of efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA intends the TSCA reporting approach to complement, not duplicate, state well-by-well disclosure programs and other existing sources of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate reporting and disclosure emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA expects the TSCA proposal would focus on providing aggregate pictures of the chemical substances and mixtures used in hydraulic fracturing rather than duplicating well-by-well disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to provide aggregate summaries that maximize transparency and public understanding while complementing state-level detailed disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide ample opportunity for dialogue and public input
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA intends to provide ample opportunity for dialogue and input about the design and scope of TSCA reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public input will be solicited through stakeholder meetings and formal notice-and-comment processes (e.g., advance notice of proposed rulemaking) to shape the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM) identifying key issues
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate public comment, EPA will publish an advance notice of proposed rulemaking identifying key issues for further discussion and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ANPRM is the first formal public step to identify issues and gather input that will inform the design and scope of any subsequent proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation to hydraulic fracturing chemicals (denial of broader E&P request)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA denied the petition's request to invoke TSCA authorities to collect information on chemicals used in the E&P sector beyond those used in hydraulic fracturing, while stating it will continue to review chemicals used in the E&P sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The immediate rulemaking focus will be on hydraulic fracturing chemicals; broader E&P-wide requirements were not adopted at this time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with states, industry, and public interest groups as full partners
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will include states, industry and public interest groups as full partners in the stakeholder discussions about reporting design and scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This coordination is intended to ensure the approach leverages existing state work, addresses stakeholders' concerns about burden, and improves public confidence and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use information gathering to inform EPA proposals (purpose of effort)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will gather information through the stakeholder process and ANPRM to inform a subsequent TSCA proposal aimed at obtaining data on chemicals used in hydraulic fracturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA frames these efforts as informational and preparatory steps to shape a proposal that balances data needs, burden minimization, and transparency objectives.
